jonny-desktop.task: context-keeper: task-aware session-start injection (bias by the files you are actually touching) + enforced_by pointer on constraints
jonny-desktop.note: DONE + PUSHED + PR OPEN, CI GREEN, AWAITING MERGE. context-keeper PR #11 on feat/task-aware-injection, 4/4 jobs green (ubuntu + windows, py3.10 + 3.12). 354 tests passing, up from 331. (1) Task-aware session-start injection: work_focus.py derives what the session is about from uncommitted paths, falling back to the last 5 commits on a clean tree, and appends a "Rules covering what you are working on" block naming constraints scoped to those paths. This is dec-005's scope_guard idea moved from edit time to session start. Critical design constraint respected: the injected block is deterministically ordered for prompt-cache stability, so focus is APPENDED after everything stable and after truncation, never ranked in among the constraints - a test asserts the stable block remains a literal prefix. Interleaving would invalidate the cache on every file touched, costing more than the irrelevance it fixes. (2) enforced_by: optional pointer naming the test that checks a constraint; verify_quality confirms the name resolves and drift details say "run X" instead of "go read the code". NEVER executed, with a test proving a command-shaped value does not fire - import_snapshot pulls from git and mirror pulls from a Worker, so an executable field would be a code-execution path into an offline store. Schema cost measured against con-004 first: +28 tokens, 2927 to 2955, 195 headroom left. THREE BUGS THE TESTS CAUGHT, all would have shipped silently: _norm used lstrip("./") which strips CHARACTERS not a prefix, so .context/ became context/ and any entry scoped to a dotfile path could never match - the same bug was already live in code_drift.py from the earlier merge and is fixed there too; git status collapses an untracked directory to "hooks/" so a brand-new file never matched a file-scoped constraint, needs -uall; and reading the summary dirtied the tree it reads because usage.record() writes .context/usage.json, so generating a summary changed the focus signal for the next one - two features built the same day interfering with each other. Dogfooded mid-edit on this repo: with server.py uncommitted it surfaced con-004, the token-budget rule this very PR had to measure itself against. NOT BUILT, remaining from the analysis: verify against a commit SHA rather than a timestamp, which would remove clock-skew/rebase fuzziness from drift.
